Scrape health (lowest target): Lowest Prometheus up value among the selected scrape jobs: 1 means all reported targets are up; 0 means at least one scrape failed. Some remote-write pipelines omit up, so no samples is not proof that targets are healthy.
API requests / second: HTTP requests handled per second across selected processes, including API and health endpoints. Use route panels below to identify which endpoints drive traffic.
API P95 request duration: 95th-percentile HTTP handler duration across selected processes. This is API server latency, not full model generation time.
Request Rate: HTTP requests per second by route and method. Health checks and monitoring requests can account for a large share of traffic.
Request Duration: HTTP request latency from histogram observations, grouped as shown in the legend. Inference streaming can outlive the HTTP handler's recorded duration.
Error Rate: HTTP responses classified as errors per second. Compare affected routes and response codes with traffic before interpreting a spike.
Top Slowest Routes (P95): Routes with the highest 95th-percentile HTTP request duration. Low-volume routes can have unstable percentile estimates.
Request Rate by Status Code: HTTP request rate grouped by response status code. A provider failure after streaming headers may still have an HTTP 200 status; use logical proxy outcomes for those failures.
Event Loop Lag (P50, P90, P99): Delay before Node.js can run scheduled work, by process and percentile. Sustained lag indicates the event loop is busy or blocked.
GC time per second: Seconds spent in garbage collection per elapsed second, displayed as a proportion. Sustained collection pressure can increase request latency.
Heap Usage by Space: Node.js heap bytes by V8 memory space. Compare sustained growth with garbage collection rather than treating every increase as a leak.
Active Handles & Requests: Node.js handles and requests still active in each process, such as sockets and filesystem operations. These are runtime objects, not the number of user API calls.
Process CPU cores used: CPU seconds consumed per elapsed second by each process. A value of 1 represents one fully used CPU core.
Memory Usage: Process memory in bytes, grouped by the memory category in the legend. Resident memory includes more than the JavaScript heap.
Process Uptime: Elapsed time since each process started. A drop indicates a restart or a different scrape target.
Active Tasks: Background tasks currently executing. This is task-queue work, separate from Agent Runtime task health.
Total Enqueued: Background tasks added during the selected period. A task can be retried later; this is not a unique user-request count.
Total Completed: Background tasks completed during the selected period, across selected processes.
Dead-Lettered: Tasks moved to the dead-letter state during the selected period after exhausting their retry policy. Inspect task failures when this rises.
Stuck Tasks Reset: Tasks whose stale execution claim was reset during the selected period so they could be retried. Repeated resets can indicate worker interruptions.
Task Throughput: Background task events per second by outcome. Compare arrivals and completions to identify accumulating work.
Task Processing Duration (P95): 95th-percentile duration of background task execution, grouped as shown. This does not measure time spent waiting in the queue.
Active Tasks Over Time: Background tasks executing at each scrape, by task type or process. Counts describe concurrent work, not throughput.
Failed & Dead Tasks: Failed task attempts and dead-letter transitions per second. A retried task can contribute more than one failure.
Active Connections: PostgreSQL connections reported by the selected external database exporter. Requires that exporter; it is separate from the application's client pool.
Max Connections: PostgreSQL's configured connection ceiling from the selected database exporter. This is server capacity, not the application's pool size.
Connection Utilization: Reported PostgreSQL connections as a percentage of the server's configured connection ceiling. Missing exporter data remains unknown.
WAL Size: Write-ahead log size reported by the PostgreSQL exporter, in bytes. This panel requires database metrics outside Archestra's application scrape.
Active Connections Over Time: PostgreSQL connection counts over time, grouped by database or connection state as exported. Compare with the server connection ceiling.
Transactions: PostgreSQL transactions per second, split by commits and rollbacks. Application retries can increase transaction volume without increasing user traffic.
Cache Hit Ratio: Share of database block accesses served from PostgreSQL's buffer cache. This is database caching, not LLM prompt caching.
Row Operations: PostgreSQL row operations per second, grouped by operation. Requires database-exporter statistics.
Locks by Mode: PostgreSQL locks by lock mode and database. Counts alone do not prove blocking; correlate with latency and database activity.
Deadlocks: PostgreSQL deadlocks per second. Any sustained increase warrants investigation of conflicting transactions.
Temp Bytes Written: Temporary data written by PostgreSQL per second, often from sorts or hashes that spill to disk. Requires a database exporter.
Database client pool connections: Application-owned database connections by pool state. Idle connections remain open for reuse; waiting work can indicate pool saturation.
Configured pool capacity: Maximum client connections configured for each application's database pool. Each process owns its own pool.
Working tasks: Runtime tasks currently working, including tasks waiting for input or authentication. Conditions overlap; replicas reporting the same configured agent are deduplicated.
Submitted tasks: Runtime tasks submitted but not yet working. A sustained count can indicate provisioning delays or unavailable runtime capacity.
Waiting for input: Runtime tasks waiting for a person to respond. These tasks can also be included in Working tasks.
Waiting for authentication: Runtime tasks that need authentication before continuing. These tasks can also be included in Working tasks.
Completions pending delivery: Completed runtime tasks whose final response has not yet been delivered. A sustained count can indicate a delivery problem.
Failures in the last 15 minutes: Failed runtime tasks and rejected scheduled launches observed in the last 15 minutes. This rolling window is independent of the dashboard time range.
Age of last successful fleet snapshot: Seconds since the newest successful runtime health snapshot in the selected period. The age keeps growing after a failed scrape; no sample means no successful snapshot is available in that period.
Oldest task heartbeat: Age in seconds of the oldest heartbeat among runtime tasks. A fresh heartbeat shows orchestration liveness, not proof that model or tool work is progressing.
Oldest undelivered completion: Age in seconds of the oldest runtime completion still awaiting delivery. Investigate delivery errors if this continues rising.
Attention by agent and backend: Nonzero runtime task conditions by configured agent and backend. Replicas are deduplicated; conditions overlap and must not be added to estimate unique tasks.
Runs reaching running / second: Agent Runtime runs that reached a running backend per second. Provisioning failures before that point are excluded.
Successful provisioning duration (P95): 95th-percentile time to provision runs that successfully reached running, including scheduling and image pulls. Failed provisioning does not contribute a successful duration observation.
Completion delivery outcomes: Final-response delivery attempts per second by interface and outcome. Retries can produce multiple attempts for one completion.
Runtime boundary refusals: Runtime crossings refused or held per second, grouped by reason. These are boundary events, not a count of unique conversations or all policy rule checks.
Steering messages / second: Messages delivered into running agent sessions per second, grouped by steering mode.
Pending export outcomes: Runtime file-export events per second by outcome, including admitted, held, and failed cleanup events. One export can have more than one lifecycle event.
Sandbox command outcomes: Code sandbox commands per second by outcome. These are command executions, not agent runs or inference calls.
Sandbox engine failures: Sandbox runtime errors per second by bounded error code. An engine-unreachable error is distinct from an individual command failure.
Sandbox runtime state by replica: Current sandbox runtime state for each process. The active state is 1; inactive states are 0, and different replicas may report different states.
Tool Calls by MCP Server: MCP tool calls per second by server, within the selected agent, server, and tool filters. This measures tool execution rather than inference requests.
Errors by MCP Server: Failed MCP tool calls per second by server, within the selected tool filters. Compare with each server's total call rate to distinguish volume from reliability.
Documents without extracted text: Documents whose ingestion produced no usable text, per second. Series appear after this event is recorded; absence does not prove every document has text.
OCR outcomes: Pages processed through OCR per second by connector and outcome. Empty panels can mean no documents required OCR.
Permission synchronization: Document permission synchronization events per second by connector and status. This is ingestion access synchronization, not a request authorization decision.
Dropped permission principals: Permission principals omitted during synchronization per second, grouped by connector and reason. Investigate unexpected drops before relying on document access parity.
Search lane timeouts: Search lane timeouts per second by lane. Connector filters do not apply because this metric has no connector label.
Quote verification: Quote verification events per second by result. Series appear when retrieval uses quote verification; connector and search-type filters do not apply.
Metered estimate in selected period: Estimated metered inference cost accrued during the selected period at configured model prices. This is not an invoice and excludes subscription-covered equivalents.
Gross cache-read savings: Estimated savings from prompt-cache reads during the selected period. Gross savings do not subtract cache-write surcharges.
Estimated spend by model: Estimated inference cost during the selected period, grouped by model. Uses configured prices rather than provider invoices.
Estimated spend by agent: Configured agents with the largest estimated inference cost during the selected period. The top ten are shown after applying cost filters.
Cache tokens in selected period: Prompt-cache tokens read and written during the selected period. These tokens are tracked separately from uncached input and output tokens.
Rule evaluations / second: Limit rule evaluations per second by enforcement behavior and outcome. One request may evaluate several rules, so this is not a request rate.
Hard rule refusals / second: Hard-limit evaluations that blocked admission per second, grouped by target type and allowance kind. Unknown spend can also cause a hard refusal.
Soft exceeded evaluations / second: Soft-limit checks that found an exhausted allowance per second. These observations do not block requests and are not unique threshold crossings.
Limit storage failures / second: Failures reading or recording limit usage per second by operation. Storage failures are separate from exhausted allowances.
Usage at last exceeded check: token_cost: Recorded USD usage at the newest known exhausted spend check for each rule and target. Selects the same replica as that check's timestamp; this is historical, not current spend.
Usage at last exceeded check: tokens: Recorded token usage at the newest known exhausted token check for each rule and target. Selects the same replica as that check's timestamp; this is historical, not live headroom.
Usage at last exceeded check: requests: Recorded request usage before admission at the newest known exhausted request check. The rejected request is excluded; this is a historical observation.
Dispatches in selected period: Logical embedded OpenAPPA hook dispatches completed during the selected period, including errors. A dispatch is counted once after internal policy-revision retries.
Failed dispatches in selected period: Embedded hook dispatches that rejected with an error during the selected period. Structured deny and refuse decisions are counted separately.
P95 tool-call hook duration: 95th-percentile wall time of embedded tool-call hooks, including consult waits and internal retries. Shared batch preloading and principal lookup occur before this timer.
Decisions / second: Embedded hook dispatches per second by hook and returned decision. Lifecycle acknowledgments such as ack or context are not policy allows.
Duration by hook (P95): 95th-percentile embedded dispatch wall time by hook. Consults, storage, and internal retries are included; this is not the duration of one policy rule.
Structured denials and refusals: Embedded dispatches returning deny_call, block, or refuse per second. These are structured outcomes rather than dispatch errors or unique denied user requests.
Tool proposal decisions: Standalone OpenAPPA tool-proposal decisions per second by outcome. Requires the standalone daemon's OTLP metrics pipeline; Archestra's embedded scrape does not publish this family.
Policy check duration (P95): 95th-percentile policy-check duration from the standalone OpenAPPA daemon. Requires its separate OTLP metrics pipeline.
External consult outcomes: Standalone helper, annotator, or authority consults per second by role and outcome. These metrics do not come from Archestra's embedded host scrape.
Remedy attempts: Standalone OpenAPPA remedy attempts per second by outcome. Requires standalone daemon telemetry.
Runtime failures by component: Standalone OpenAPPA runtime failures per second by component and bounded error type. Requires its separate OTLP metrics pipeline.
Standalone runtime uptime: Elapsed uptime in seconds for each standalone OpenAPPA daemon instance. A drop indicates a restart; this is separate from Archestra process uptime.
Requests / second: Logical inference requests completed per second, including successful and non-success outcomes. Provider and logical-request filters apply; upstream model and agent filters do not.
P95 full request duration: 95th-percentile logical inference request duration, from handler entry through preflight, retries, and complete streaming. Model and agent filters do not apply.
Requests in selected period: Logical inference requests completed during the selected period, including errors, denials, and cancellations. This excludes failures before requests reach the inference handler.
Outcomes / second: Logical inference request rate by final outcome, including midstream failures after HTTP 200 headers. Model and agent filters do not apply.
Operational errors and throttles: Logical inference failures per second by error origin and outcome, separating provider, platform, and client failures. Policy denials and incomplete generation are shown separately.
Denials, cancellations and incomplete re: Logical inference requests per second ending in a policy or limit denial, client cancellation, or incomplete provider generation. These outcomes must not be treated as successful completions.
Full request latency by provider (P95): 95th-percentile logical inference duration by resolved provider. Router admission failures may be attributed to router before a provider is selected.
First upstream chunk (P95): 95th-percentile time from the upstream request to its first streaming chunk. This excludes work before Archestra initiates the provider call.
Tokens / second: Uncached input and output tokens consumed per second. Prompt-cache reads and writes are recorded separately.
Cached tokens / second: Prompt-cache tokens read or written per second. Cache support and reporting vary by provider.
Upstream calls by model: Upstream duration observations per second by model. Retries can add observations, so this is not a unique logical request count.
Upstream calls by agent: Configured agents with the highest upstream call rate after filters. Retries can add observations; only the top ten are shown.
